name: Question 11
problem: At which points on the surface $z={x}^{3}+xy$ is the tangent plane horizontal?
worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z=f(x,y)$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ on the surface can be written as

$$
z-{z}_{0}=(x-{x}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂x}({x}_{0},{y}_{0})+(y-{y}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂y}({x}_{0},{y}_{0}),
$$

where $⟨\frac{∂f}{∂x}({x}_{0},{y}_{0}),\frac{∂f}{∂y}({x}_{0},{y}_{0}),-1⟩$ represents a normal vector to the tangent plane.

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}+xy)=3{x}^{2}+y \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}+xy)=x\end{aligned}
$$

 

Hence, the normal vector to the tangent plane is 

$$
⟨3{x}^{2}+y,\,x,\,-1⟩.
$$

Note that the tangent plane is horizontal if and only if the normal vector is vertical. This means that the $x$- and $y$-components of the vector must be $0:$

$$
{\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=0 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y}=0\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}+y=0 \\ x=0\end{aligned}
$$

 

From the second equation we get $x=0.$ Substituting $x=0$ into first equation, we obtain $y=0.$

Finally, substituting $x=0$ and $y=0$ into our function, we get

$$
z={0}^{3}+0(0)=0.
$$

Therefore, the point where the tangent plane is horizontal is $(0,0,0).$

Question 11
?

At which points on the surface z=x3+xy is the tangent plane horizontal?

a
(0,0,0) only
b
(0,0,0) and (1,1,2)
c
(−1,1,−2) only
d
(1,1,2) only
e
(−1,1,−2) and (1,1,2)
Submit
Correct

The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the surface z=f(x,y) at the point (x0,y0,z0) on the surface can be written as z−z0=(x−x0)∂f∂x(x0,y0)+(y−y0)∂f∂y(x0,y0), where ⟨∂f∂x(x0,y0),∂f∂y(x0,y0),−1⟩ represents a normal vector to the tangent plane.

First, we find the partial derivatives: ∂f∂x=∂∂x(x3+xy)=3x2+y∂f∂y=∂∂y(x3+xy)=x

Hence, the normal vector to the tangent plane is ⟨3x2+y,x,−1⟩.

Note that the tangent plane is horizontal if and only if the normal vector is vertical. This means that the x- and y-components of the vector must be 0: {∂f∂x=0∂f∂y=0⟹{3x2+y=0x=0

From the second equation we get x=0. Substituting x=0 into first equation, we obtain y=0.

Finally, substituting x=0 and y=0 into our function, we get z=03+0(0)=0.

Therefore, the point where the tangent plane is horizontal is (0,0,0).
